keyVerseText: For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.
rootMeaning: The root of כַּלְכֹּל (Kalkôl) traces back to כּוּל (kûwl), which carries the fundamental idea of sustaining, nourishing, and providing. This root implies the capacity to hold, contain, and maintain, going beyond a mere name to suggest a role or quality of provision and endurance. The etymology rooted in sustenance enriches the understanding of the word by linking it to the vital concept of support and preservation, which is foundational both physically and spiritually.
usageInScripture: The word כַּלְכֹּל appears only twice in Scripture, always as a proper name referring to an individual, specifically one of the wise men compared to Solomon. It is translated consistently as 'and Chalcol' or 'and Calcol,' indicating its function as a personal name rather than a common noun. This limited but consistent usage highlights the word's unique identity tied to wisdom and heritage rather than a broader lexical range.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding כַּלְכֹּל as a name derived from a root meaning 'sustaining' invites reflection on the providential and sustaining wisdom that God grants to His people. As one of the wise men with whom Solomon was compared, Chalcol symbolizes the God-ordained capacity to nurture and uphold truth and righteousness. This insight encourages believers to see wisdom not only as intellectual ability but as a sustaining grace from God that nourishes faith and life. It reminds the church that true wisdom is a divine provision, sustaining the community and individual believers in their walk with Christ.
keyVerseReflection: 1 Kings 4:31 highlights Solomon's unparalleled wisdom, stating he was wiser than Ethan, Heman, Chalcol, and Darda, renowned wise men of their time. The mention of Chalcol here, a name rooted in sustaining provision, emphasizes the surpassing nature of Solomon's God-given wisdom. It shows that even the greatest human wisdom, represented by Chalcol, is ultimately eclipsed by the divine wisdom bestowed upon Solomon, pointing to the ultimate source of sustaining knowledge and understanding in God.
